title: SRE comms timeline playbook - quickref
content:
Purpose:
Provide a compact, easy-to-scan runbook for incident communications and war‑room behavior. Focus is rapid, consistent updates across status page, customer channels, and internal war‑room. This is a working draft intended for on-call SREs, support leads, and the comms owner during incidents.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: communications and immediate runbook (T0 → T+4h) for platform availability, degraded performance, and data-sensitivity incidents.
- Audience: on-call SRE, incident commander, comms lead, support/CSM, legal (if P0/P1 with customer-data impact).

Quick timeline (T0 anchor = incident detection or pager):
- T0 (detection / pager fires):
  - Incident commander (IC) ack and set Slack war-room channel: #incident-{incident_id}
  - Post initial short Slack: "P{sev} {service} incident detected. IC: @name. Triage in progress. Status page: updating."
  - Create incident record (Jira/ops ticket) and add link to Slack.

- T+5m:
  - Confirm severity and primary impact statement (one-sentence).
  - Comms lead drafts first public status page entry (short form).
  - Support lead notifies active customers on impacted plans (CSM rapid list).

- T+15m:
  - Post first status page update (short).
  - Internal update: root cause hypothesis if available, mitigation underway? yes/no.
  - Log actions taken in incident ticket timeline.

- T+30m to T+60m:
  - Regular cadence updates (see cadence below).
  - If mitigated, escalate to validation and customer verification.
  - If unresolved, expand comms to broader stakeholders (sales, legal, exec) as required per impact checklist.

- T+2h onward:
  - Maintain cadence and indicate next ETA for follow-up.
  - Plan handoff if incident spans shifts (use handoff template).

Status page templates (short then expanded):
- Minimal fields on each entry: incident_id, impacted services, started_at, status (investigating/identified/monitoring/resolved), summary, updates (timestamped).

- P1 example (short):
  - Short: "Major outage affecting API responses for some customers. Engineers investigating. No workaround yet. Next update in 30m."
  - Expanded (first public post):
    - Title: "API generation failures affecting requests to /v1/generate"
    - Impact: "Customers may receive 500 responses or timeouts for API calls in US-west region."
    - Current status: "Investigating — service degraded"
    - What we're doing: "Rolling back recent deploy, collecting traces, scaling replicas"
    - ETA/next update: "Next update 30 minutes"

- P2 example (short):
  - "Intermittent increased latency for embeddings endpoints. Partial mitigation applied. Monitoring."

- P3 example (short):
  - "Minor errors for a small subset of requests; workaround available."

Update cadence guidance (recommended):
- P1: every 15–30 minutes while active, or immediately when a material change occurs.
- P2: every 30–60 minutes.
- P3: every 2–4 hours or on resolution.

Customer-facing email: (use only when incident materially affects SLAs/customers or when asked by CSM/legal)
- Subject (P1): "Service outage affecting Redwood API — {short impact} — Incident {incident_id}"
- Body template:
  - Greeting, quick summary: "We're investigating an outage affecting {service}. Some requests are failing or timing out."
  - Impact: "Impacted customers: {list/segment}. Approx start: {started_at}."
  - Current status & actions: "Our engineers are {action} and we've taken {mitigation}."
  - Advice & temporary workarounds: "If you see X, try Y; otherwise we will update the status page."
  - Contact & ETA: "Support ticket: {link}. Next update: {ETA}."
  - Signoff: "— Redwood Inference Support"

Support portal / CSM notification blurb (short):
- "We are currently investigating an issue impacting {service} that may affect {customer_segment}. Please monitor the status page: {link}. For urgent questions, reply to this ticket or reach your CSM."

Internal war-room checklist (first 30 minutes):
1) Establish command & channel:
   - Create #incident-{incident_id} channel and invite IC, comms lead, SRE on-call, support lead, product owner.
2) Single-thread principle:
   - All public statements come from the comms lead and the status page. Avoid multiple concurrent external posts.
3) Record basics in incident ticket:
   - start time, detection method, initial pager, impacted services, hypothesis, links (traces, logs, dashboards).
4) Evidence capture:
   - Snapshot traces, recent deploy IDs, config changes, autoscaling events, KV cache stats. Attach to ticket.
5) Mitigation experiments (document thoroughly):
   - Who did what and when (command + exact commands). If rollback used, add commit hash.
6) Customer impact triage:
   - Is customer data exposed? If yes, alert security/legal immediately.
7) Comms cadence & owner assignment:
   - Assign comms lead and cadence (15m/30m).
8) Escalation rules:
   - If incident >2h with no stable mitigation, notify ops director and sales leadership. If data exposure, notify Privacy Officer immediately.
9) Handoff intent:
   - If passing to next shift, prepare a 10-minute briefing and update ticket with open actions.

Roles & responsibilities (short):
- Incident Commander (IC): orchestrates, owns decision to escalate and severity.
- Comms Lead: drafts and posts status page & customer notes, coordinates external comms.
- SRE Lead / On-call: drives technical diagnosis, documents mitigations.
- Support Lead: surfaces affected customers, opens CS tickets, coordinates CSMs.
- Security/Legal: only if P0/P1 involving data/PII.

Noise control and message hygiene:
- Prefer short, consistent phrasing across channels.
- Use the status page as the source of truth for customer-facing state.
- If a Slack message is posted, include the status page link and timestamp.
- Close broken threads: move technical commentary to the incident ticket and summarize key findings in Slack.

PII / sensitive incidents rules:
- Do not include customer identifiers in public status posts. Use generic descriptors ("some customers in EU region").
- For legal/regulated incidents, redact logs before sharing externally. Comms lead to coordinate with Security for wording.

Handoff template (for shift change):
- Incident ID: {incident_id}
- Current status: {investigating/identified/monitoring}
- Last update: {timestamp}
- Primary hypothesis: {short}
- Actions in flight: {list}
- Next ETA for update: {time}
- Owner for next steps: {name}

Post-incident follow-up checklist:
- Send final status update & short customer note within 24h of resolution.
- Schedule postmortem within 3 business days; assign author.
- Include: timeline (second-resolution granularity), root cause analysis, mitigations, action owner + target dates.
- Communicate major follow-ups to sales and customer success if customers impacted SLAs.

Examples (realistic snippets):
- Slack initial (T0):
  - "[P1][investigating] API generation errors in us-west. IC: @Ethan. Evidence collected; linking ticket SRE-421. Status page: {link}."

- Status page short update (T+15):
  - "Investigating — Intermittent 500 errors on /v1/generate for some customers in us-west. Engineers are reverting a recent deploy while we validate. Next update in 30 minutes."

- Public final note (post-resolve):
  - "Resolved — The API errors were caused by a bad model shard rollout. We rolled back the deploy at {time} and metrics returned to normal. Root cause and long-term fix scheduled in SRE-431; we will follow up with impacted customers."

Open questions / draft items to resolve in this doc:
- Exact branching for CSM/customer outreach by plan tier (who contacts enterprise vs self-serve).
- Template approval flow for customer-facing emails when legal review is required.
- Integrations with statuspage provider for automated updates (investigate API rate limits).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally compact so it can be printed/pinned in the war-room. Add examples or reword for our legal/comms review.

End of quickref.
